# How much must particle masses change across a SPARC galaxy?

For unscreened matter with m = m₀ A(r), the extra radial acceleration is −c² d ln A/dr.
A circular orbit therefore requires ln[A(r_out)/A(r_in)] = ∫(V_obs² − V_bar²) d ln r / c².
The endpoints are the innermost and outermost measured radii of each galaxy.

The cuts Q ≤ 2 and inclination ≥ 30° select 153 of 175 galaxies. At 3.6 μm we fix the disk and bulge
mass-to-light ratios at 0.5 and 0.7 in solar units. We integrate by trapezoids in ln r,
using V_bar² = V_gas|V_gas| + Υ_disk V_disk|V_disk| + Υ_bulge V_bulge|V_bulge|.
[Lelli et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.09251) and [McGaugh et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.05917).

## Size

| Quantity | Galaxies | Median | 16th–84th percentile | Maximum |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Δln A | 153 | 1.14e-07 | 2.71e-08–4.64e-07 | 2.05e-06 |
| Δln A / (V_flat²/c²) | 123 | 1.04 | 0.57–1.63 | 2.67 |
| Δln A / (ΔΦ_bar/c²) | 153 | 1.68 | 0.383–4.07 | 10.9 |
| g_lens / g_obs at r_out | 153 | 0.234 | 0.14–0.369 | 0.676 |

ΔΦ_bar is the integral of V_bar² over the same radii. The required mass change is comparable
to the baryonic potential difference in units of c² (median ratio 1.68).
The signed integrals include 4 nonpositive excursions. Flat-speed units require a measured V_flat > 0.
Unweighted least squares on the 120 positive pairs gives a log Δln A versus log V_flat slope of
2.05 (Pearson r = 0.89). This describes the selected sample.

The [per-galaxy results](sparc_mass_budget.json) give the linearised error from errV, assuming independent
speed errors. Each radius enters once with its full trapezoid weight. The two additional excursions shift
Υ_disk by ±0.1 dex coherently across a galaxy at fixed Υ_bulge. They show sensitivity
to the assumed disk mass. Distance, inclination and component-model systematics are outside the error bars.

## Light

Null geodesics are invariant under a conformal rescaling. If the field's own gravity is negligible, light
responds only to the baryonic metric. At the last measured radius the corresponding acceleration ratio
g_lens/g_obs = V_bar²/V_obs² has median 0.23. This is a prediction from
the rotation curves. SPARC supplies no lensing measurement here.

Independent observations find excess gravity in light deflection as well. KiDS-1000 weak lensing extends
the galaxy radial acceleration relation beyond the visible disks. Cluster lensing also requires more
gravity than the observed baryons supply. [Brouwer et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.11677) and
[Clowe et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0608407).

## Local screening

For A = 1 + φ²/(2M²) and |φ| ≤ v, the largest possible positive excursion is ln[1 + v²/(2M²)].
Covering the largest central SPARC value requires v²/(2M²) ≥ exp(Δln A_max) − 1 ≈ 2.05e-06.
This lower bound assumes the full field range is available. Solar-system screening requires a local field
solution and a comparison with local tests, both outside this repository.
[Burrage, Copeland & Millington](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.07529).

## Verdict

The integral specifies the force a mass profile would have to supply. It does not establish a field solution.
Lensing is the decisive obstacle
to replacing dark matter this way. If the field's energy supplies the missing lensing gravity,
the field itself plays the role of gravitating dark matter.
